note: Known false positives of tools/release_screen.py's content sniffer.
An entry says: this file trips the sniffer, for this reason, and the reason is
not note text. Nothing here weakens the path rules — a file must already be
publishable by path to be sniffed at all.
Rules the screener enforces on this file, so they cannot be quietly relaxed:
- Literal paths only. No wildcards, no directory prefixes. The lesson of the
data/acquire/*.sh bypass is that a whitelist keyed on anything broader than
a filename stops naming what it permits.
- Nothing under data/ or sealed/, and nothing the deny rules cover. Those are
corpus and sealed paths; a sniffer hit on one of them is the alarm, not a
nuisance. data/README.md is excluded too, even though it is publishable: it
is the one file published out of a denied prefix, so it is the last file
that should be exemptible from the content check as well.
- `sniff` pins WHICH kind of hit is expected. A file allowlisted for Korean
prose that starts tripping the clinical-header pattern is reported as
unexpected, because that is a different fact about the file.
- `why` has to be a real sentence. An entry nobody can evaluate later is an
entry that gets renewed forever.
Reasons are written in English deliberately: Korean prose in this file would
trip HANGUL_PROSE and the allowlist would need an entry for itself.

entries.why: Project instructions, written in Korean. Prose about the rules — including the rule against putting corpus text in files like this one. No corpus text.
Korean comments documenting the identifier vocabulary. The values are experiment identifiers; the prose explains what each axis is for.
Korean comments explaining the error-sample parameters and why changing them invalidates a port-human run. Holds four integers and two strings; no span, no offset, no corpus text.
Korean comments explaining the corpora: and sealed: keys. This is the committed template and holds no real path; the machine's real paths live in data_paths.local.yaml, which is gitignored.
This is the file that searches for that header, and its own docstring and CLINICAL_HEADER pattern quote it. Self-match, present since the first version.
The NOTE constant is a synthetic MIMIC-shaped header, invented for the test that proves the sniffer catches one. It comes from no corpus, which is why it can be committed.
